questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 98°. What is the co-interior (allied) angle on the other parallel line?
questions.why: Co-interior (allied) angles sum to 180°, so 180° − 98° = 82°. A common mistake is thinking they're equal like alternate angles, but co-interior angles are supplementary, not equal.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has sides of length 7 cm, 7 cm, and 7 cm. What type of triangle is this?
questions.why: All three sides equal means equilateral, which also gives three equal 60° angles. Isosceles only requires two equal sides, so it's a common mix-up to call an equilateral triangle isosceles instead of naming it most specifically.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Solve for x: 5(x − 1) = 20. What is x?
questions.why: Divide both sides by 5 first to get x − 1 = 4, then add 1 to both sides to get x = 5. A common slip is subtracting 1 before dividing, treating the −1 as if it weren't inside the bracket.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: In human reproduction, what is the main role of the sperm cell?
options: To carry the male's genetic material to fertilise the egg
To provide all the nutrients for the growing embryo
To produce the placenta after fertilisation
To control the release of eggs from the ovary
questions.answer: To carry the male's genetic material to fertilise the egg
questions.why: The sperm's job is to deliver genetic material to the egg during fertilisation. Nutrients for the embryo come from the mother via the placenta, not from the sperm — a common confusion of roles.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Blitz ⚡ Which year did the First Crusade set out to try to capture Jerusalem?
questions.why: The First Crusade began in 1096. Students sometimes confuse this with 1215 (Magna Carta) or 1066 (Norman Conquest), which are different key medieval dates entirely.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: A historian writes: 'Years of unfair taxation built resentment among peasants, and this resentment finally exploded into revolt after a new tax was announced.' Which part is the long-term cause?
options: Years of unfair taxation building resentment
questions.answer: Years of unfair taxation building resentment
questions.why: Long-term causes build up over time (like years of unfair taxation), while the trigger (the new tax) is the short-term spark. Students often mistake the trigger for the whole cause, missing the deeper build-up.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Magna Carta 1215 established which key principle about the monarch's power?
options: The king was not above the law and had to follow it too
The king could tax the barons without any limits
The king had unlimited power over the church
The king could imprison anyone without reason
questions.answer: The king was not above the law and had to follow it too
questions.why: Magna Carta's key legacy is that even the king was subject to the law, limiting arbitrary royal power. Some assume it gave the king MORE power, but it was actually a check against him.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: A student investigates whether the amount of caffeine (in mg) affects reaction time (measured in milliseconds), keeping the time of day and the person's sleep the same for each test. Which is the dependent variable?
questions.why: The dependent variable is what you MEASURE as a result — here, reaction time. The amount of caffeine is what you deliberately change (independent variable), and time of day and sleep are kept the same (controlled variables). Mixing up 'what changes' with 'what you measure' is the classic confident-wrong trap.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 47°. What is the alternate angle on the other parallel line?
questions.why: Alternate angles are equal when formed by a transversal crossing parallel lines — they form a 'Z' shape. A common error is adding to 180° as if they were co-interior angles instead.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A quadrilateral has one pair of parallel sides that are not equal in length, and the other two sides are equal (not parallel). What is the most specific name for this shape?
questions.why: An isosceles trapezium has exactly one pair of parallel sides and the non-parallel sides are equal in length. Calling it a parallelogram is wrong because a parallelogram needs TWO pairs of parallel sides.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: During sexual reproduction, offspring inherit genetic material from how many parents, and how does this affect genetic variation compared to asexual reproduction?
options: Two parents, creating more genetic variation than asexual reproduction
Two parents, creating identical clones like asexual reproduction
One parent, creating more genetic variation than asexual reproduction
questions.answer: Two parents, creating more genetic variation than asexual reproduction
questions.why: Sexual reproduction combines genetic material from two parents, producing offspring that are genetically different from both parents and each other. Asexual reproduction uses only one parent and produces genetically identical clones — this contrast is the key exam point.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: Your classmate says: 'In an experiment testing how the type of fertiliser affects crop yield, the number of plants tested is the independent variable, because that's what the scientist decides to use.' Using a different example of your own (not fertiliser, sleep, sunlight, water temperature, or soil type), explain what actually makes a variable 'independent', 'dependent', or 'controlled', and correct your classmate's misunderstanding.
